title: Lightweight Latch and Hinge Hardware for the Overhead Stowage Compartments
abstract: A magnesium-alloy latch and hinge set for the overhead stowage compartments, studied to recover cabin mass on payload-limited networks. Cancelled at the design review after the flammability and corrosion case failed to close.

sections.reason: Several operators on thin long-haul networks asked for cabin mass reduction, and the stowage compartment latch and hinge hardware was one of the few remaining items with a meaningful mass fraction that could be changed without touching the certified compartment structure. A magnesium-alloy latch and hinge set offered about eighty kilogrammes per aircraft across a full shipset, which was enough to remove a winter payload restriction on the routes the operators named.
sections.description: The study covered a magnesium-alloy replacement for the monument fitting D2520125508153 and the associated hinge trim D2520122039443, retained by floating barrel nuts AES161226K4 in the existing compartment structure. The compartment shell, the gas strut and the certified load path were to remain unchanged, and the latch interface geometry was held identical so that no cabin crew retraining would be needed. Work would have been done in zones 222 and 262 during a cabin visit, one compartment at a time. The stowage insert 851DL would have been refitted without change.
sections.effects: The projected mass reduction was 78 kg per shipset with no electrical or balance consequence and no change to the compartment load rating. Against that, the flammability substantiation for a magnesium alloy inside the cabin required a full-scale test campaign that had not been budgeted, and the corrosion case in the presence of galley spillage could not be closed with the surface treatment proposed by the supplier. The pre-analysis recorded both as blocking and the design review cancelled the change rather than fund the test campaign.
sections.embodiment_note: Cancelled at the design review of February 2025. No embodiment point, no Service Bulletin and no spares. The requesting operator has been given the written position it asked for and the file is retained so that the same question is not reopened without new evidence.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, no reportable CG shift
type_data.production_impact: None, cancelled before any production commitment
